user.title: Dashboard Assistant
user.description: Enter the address and API token of your Dashboard Assistant device. The device never displays its token — it is the api_token from the dashboard-assistant.yaml seed file you provisioned it with. Leave this to pairing instead if you can.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Dashboard Assistant
zeroconf_confirm.description: Add {name}? Pair automatically so you don't have to copy the token, or enter it by hand.

pair.title: Pair with {name}
pair.description: Couldn't pair automatically. A device only pairs once, so an already-adopted device refuses to hand out its token again — remove its old Home Assistant entry, or factory-reset the device from its admin page, then retry. (A brand-new device pairs on its own.)

manual.title: Dashboard Assistant
manual.description: Enter {name}'s API token — the api_token from the dashboard-assistant.yaml seed file it was provisioned with. The device never displays it.

reauth_confirm.title: Dashboard Assistant
reauth_confirm.description: The device could not be verified. This usually means it was factory-reset, which regenerates both its API token and its security certificate. Enter the current api_token from its dashboard-assistant.yaml seed file, or remove this entry and re-add the device to pair again.

error.pairing_closed: This device has already been paired. Remove its existing Home Assistant entry, or factory-reset the device from its admin page, then try again.
error.cert_mismatch: This device is presenting a different security certificate than the one Home Assistant recorded when it was added. That is expected if it has been factory-reset. If it has not been, something on your network may be impersonating it.

abort.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach the device to identify it — it may still be starting up. It will be rediscovered automatically.
abort.wrong_device: The token belongs to a different Dashboard Assistant device
